title: Environment Setup and Console Tour
html:
Goal: get your team's console address and the passwords of the five accounts from the organiser, sign in to Launchpad console V3 as admin, handle the first-visit onboarding, set the rail to show every module, confirm in the browser that the environment is ready, and learn where each module sits on the Agent-DLC flywheel.

Prerequisites

  • A modern browser (Chrome / Edge / Firefox / Safari). The whole workshop happens in the browser: you do not need an AWS account, the AWS console, CloudShell, access keys or any AWS credentials, and your laptop does not need the AWS CLI, Node.js or Python.
  • The organiser has deployed your team's environment in advance and given your team one ConsoleUrl and the passwords of five accounts (see section 1).
  • This whole chapter uses the admin account. admin is the console's built-in administrator. It owns the environment itself (accounts, workspaces, release policy) and takes no part in building or signing later on, which is what lets the Roles chapter demonstrate separation of duties.

This workshop runs in us-east-1 (US East (N. Virginia)) only: every team's environment is deployed in us-east-1, and the console shows the Region us-east-1 throughout.

1. Get your team's access details from the organiser

Before the event, the organiser (the facilitator or event owner) deploys a separate environment for every team: one AWS account and one console per team. Your team receives the following (usually as a table or a direct message):

Item Content Used in
ConsoleUrl Your team's console address, like https://dxxxxxxxxxxxx.cloudfront.net Everywhere. Every chapter happens in a browser on this address
admin password The console's built-in administrator This chapter, the Roles chapter, and every later admin step
developer password Developer: builds, deploys, drafts criteria, starts evaluations and release requests The Roles chapter onwards
biz-owner password Business owner: signs criteria, curates the golden set, decides judge calibration The Roles chapter onwards
release-ops password Release operator: signs releases, approves waivers, rolls back The Roles chapter onwards
sme password Domain expert: the second annotator The Roles chapter onwards

The five usernames are fixed: admin, developer, biz-owner, release-ops, sme. The passwords differ per team and work only on your team's ConsoleUrl.

These passwords belong to your team only. Keep them locally and do not paste them into public chat channels. When copying, avoid leading or trailing spaces.

2. What is in your environment

The organiser deploys the same CloudFormation template for every team, and it builds a secure network layout by default:

  • Network: one VPC whose public subnet holds only a NAT gateway; two private subnets hold the console instance and every agent you deploy. The console instance has no public IP, so the internet cannot reach it directly.
  • Reaching the console: a CloudFront distribution provides the HTTPS address (that is ConsoleUrl) and reaches the instance in the private subnet through a VPC origin, over the AWS network; nginx on the instance also checks the origin key header CloudFront injects.
  • Reaching AWS services: Bedrock, AgentCore, CloudWatch Logs, ECR and other services go through VPC interface endpoints, and S3 through a gateway endpoint, so that traffic stays inside the VPC. The NAT gateway is used only for the public internet (for example an agent calling a public MCP server or installing Python dependencies).
  • Preset templates: the template registered the network profile workshop-private and the S3 Files storage workshop-files and made them the default project's defaults. The default project cannot hold new agents, so the Platform configuration chapter allows them for 零售客服, the project the flywheel runs in; after that you just pick them when you create an agent, with no VPC details to fill in.
  • Initialisation: at boot the instance created Launchpad's shared infrastructure (the AgentCore Registry, Memory, Gateway and others), turned on CloudWatch Transaction Search, probed the Bedrock models with real calls, created the five console accounts, preset the release policy of the default workspace to gated (gated), and installed the online updater.
flowchart LR
  B[Your browser] -->|HTTPS| CF[CloudFront<br/>ConsoleUrl]
  subgraph VPC
    subgraph Private subnets
      NG[nginx :80] -->|/api/ and /v1/| BE[Launchpad backend :8000]
      NG -->|everything else| FE[Frontend static files]
      AG[Agents you deploy]
    end
    EP[VPC endpoints<br/>Bedrock · AgentCore · Logs · ECR · S3]
    NAT[NAT gateway<br/>public subnet]
  end
  CF -->|VPC origin + origin key header| NG
  BE --> EP
  AG --> EP
  AG -.public internet.-> NAT

The console backend reaches AWS with the instance's IAM role: every button you click in the console is the backend calling AgentCore and Bedrock on your behalf, so you need no AWS permissions yourself.

3. Sign in to console V3 as admin

3.1 Open ConsoleUrl/v3 and sign in

  1. Open ConsoleUrl/v3 in your browser (ConsoleUrl followed by /v3).
  2. The sign-in card on the right has two tabs, Sign in and Register (the Register tab means self-registration is on; the Roles chapter uses it). The 中文 / EN toggle is at the top right.
  3. On the Sign in tab enter Username admin and Password the admin password from the organiser, then click Sign in.

In the image: 1 the Sign in tab; 2 Username; 3 Password; 4 the Sign in button. Switch 中文 / EN at the top right.

Expected result: after signing in you stay on ConsoleUrl/v3, V3's Command center. The eyebrow reads COMMAND CENTER · DEFAULT · US-EAST-1 (that line is shown in capitals); on a fresh environment nothing is waiting, so the title reads "All quiet. Nothing needs you."

If you open ConsoleUrl without /v3, a fresh browser lands in console V2 (the address becomes ConsoleUrl/v2 and the top left shows a V2 badge). Open ConsoleUrl/v3 in the address bar, or click Try V3 at the top right of V2. Once you have opened any /v3 page, the browser remembers V3: reloads and a bare ConsoleUrl come back to V3. The choice is stored per browser (profile), so every new private window or browser profile has to open ConsoleUrl/v3 once.

3.2 The V3 top bar

From left to right:

Where What What it does
Top left Launchpad with a V3 badge Back to the Command center
Middle The search box "Jump to an agent, page or action…" with a ⌘K hint Opens the command palette. ⌘K (Ctrl+K on Windows / Linux) or / open it too; type a page, an agent or a term you don't know to jump there
Right The workspace selector (prefixed Workspace), showing Default · us-east-1 Decides which AWS account and Region every request targets. A DEV-tier workspace carries no extra tier label
Right The language button: EN in the Chinese UI, 中 in the English UI Switches the UI language
Right The theme button (moon / sun icon) Switches between the dark and light themes. Every screenshot in this workshop uses the dark theme
Right The help button ? Its menu holds Take the tour, Show the launch sequence, Glossary, Video guides
Right Back to V2 Switches to the V2 layout. Not used in this workshop
Right Your username admin, with the change-password and sign-out icons Sign out first when you switch accounts

In the image: 1 the command palette search (⌘K); 2 the workspace selector; 3 the language switch; 4 the theme switch; 5 the ? help menu; 6 Back to V2 (not used in this workshop); 7 the current user, change password and sign out.

Every step of this workshop happens in console V3; do not click Back to V2. Some pages V3 has not rebuilt (certain forms, editors, an agent's management detail page) open the V2 page inside V3: the address is /v2/..., but the top bar and the rail are still V3's. That is expected. If you find yourself in V2 (a V2 badge at the top left) or in the classic console, open ConsoleUrl/v3 in the address bar to return to V3.

3.3 First visit: the tour, the launch sequence and the glossary

On your first visit to the Command center, V3 offers three newcomer aids:

Console tour (opens on its own 1.2 seconds after you reach the Command center): the console dims, one area at a time is lit with a short card beside it, and the card's top left shows progress from 01 / 06 to 06 / 06. The stops:

Step Card title What is lit
1 One keystroke to anywhere The top-bar search box (command palette)
2 Your launch sequence The Command center's Launch sequence
3 What needs you The Needs you list
4 Colour means something The four stat tiles, with a colour legend: Mint running as intended, Amber waiting on someone or something, Coral it needs you, Blue in progress or just so you know, Grey off, draft or not applicable
5 Every module, grouped The Modules in the rail
6 Help is always here The top-bar help button ?

Page through with Next / Back (or the → / ← keys) and finish with Got it; Skip or Esc leaves at any point. Once finished or skipped, the tour does not open on its own again; reopen it from ? → Take the tour.

Launch sequence: the Launch sequence panel below the Command center's four metric cards (Live, Waiting, Needs you, Latency P95) lists five steps from an empty workspace to a release that waits for a signature, with a done count steps done/5 on the right. Each step ticks itself off from what actually exists, not from a click:

Step Ticks off when Chapter of this workshop
01 Workspace ready The workspace's bootstrap status is Ready This chapter (already ticked)
02 First agent live One agent is active Build
03 Talk to it An active agent has a chat session Build
04 Score it The workspace has run an evaluation Evaluate
05 Gate its releases An agent has moved to named endpoints (live) Release

Expected result: a fresh environment shows 1/5 with Workspace ready ticked and the next step, First agent live, lit. Do not click the step buttons (such as Launch one) now: the later chapters create and name the agents in a specific way, and the sequence ticks itself off as you work through them. To get it out of the way, click the × (Hide) at the panel's top right; ? → Show the launch sequence brings it back. Once all five steps are ticked (after the Release chapter), the panel folds into one line, "Launch sequence complete — this workspace builds, runs, evaluates and gates releases.", with a Hide button on the right.

Glossary: does not open on its own. Click ? → Glossary and search with Find a term; typing a term into the command palette offers a "What is …?" entry; terms with a dotted underline on a page show a one-sentence meaning on hover and open the glossary on that term when clicked. The AGENT-DLC section at the top of the glossary holds cards for the methodology's terms — criteria, criteria set, golden set, gate and the rest — and each card says where it is Used in along the storyline (click to jump there), Who owns it, and its related terms; general platform words such as Harness, Runtime and Canary follow below. For which chapter and section of this workshop uses each term, see Appendix · Glossary.

In the image: 1 Find a term; 2 an Agent-DLC term card; 3 Used in: the storyline steps that use it, click to jump.

The tour card (red box) opens on its own the first time. Page through with Next, or close it with Skip / Esc.

4. A tour of the V3 rail

The rail on the left has two parts. The four fixed entries at the top are V3's redesigned core pages; below them, Modules groups the rest along the agent lifecycle, with the number of modules after each group name. Groups start folded (except the one holding the current page); click a group name to fold or unfold it, and the browser remembers which are open. The foot of the rail shows the current workspace's Region, us-east-1.

4.1 Switch to "every module"

At the very bottom of Modules is a display-mode button. It names the mode a click switches to:

  • It reads Show every module: only the everyday modules are showing (a member account's default).
  • It reads Show the everyday modules only: every module is showing (an administrator account's default).

Later chapters use entries that only appear with every module showing, such as Registry, Memory, Governance, Evaluation tasks, Online evaluation, Evaluators and A/B experiments, so this workshop uses that mode throughout:

  1. Look at the button at the bottom of Modules. If it reads Show every module, click it.
  2. Confirm the button now reads Show the everyday modules only and the Agent evaluation group shows 9.

This is a view filter, not authorization (the button's tooltip reads "A view filter: every page stays reachable by URL and ⌘K"); the backend decides permissions per account, and the Roles chapter shows the difference. The mode is stored per browser (profile), not per account: switching accounts in the same browser keeps it, while in every new private window or browser profile a member account starts with the everyday modules only and needs one more click on Show every module.

4.2 Where each entry sits on the flywheel

The table shows the rail as admin sees it with every module showing. Unless noted, each entry opens V3's rebuilt /v3/... page:

Group Entry Address What it does Flywheel phase
(fixed) Command center /v3 What needs you, the launch sequence, traffic and the fleet —
Agents /v3/agents Every agent in this workspace and what it is doing now; a count next to the entry flags failed deploys Build
Chat /v3/chat Pick an agent and chat, thumbs up / down on answers Build, Improve
Release gate /v3/gate Red lines, then the denominator, then each dimension's threshold, then what is only observed; a passing report moves only once a person signs it Evaluate, Release
Agent development Architect assistant /v3/assistant Design an agent conversationally Build
New agent /v3/create Quick deploy of a managed Harness agent, or the full form and the other ways to build (Strands, container, BYOC and more) Build
Agent IDE /v2/coding A member's own remote codex coding repositories, deployed through BYOC (a V2 page; not used in this workshop) Build
Registry /v3/registry Registry records for agents, tools, skills Build
Knowledge Bases /v3/knowledge Managed knowledge bases and documents Build
Context layer /v2/context-layer The connected COA context layer: metrics, an ontology and documents (a V2 page; not used in this workshop) Build
Agent runtime Releases /v3/releases Cross-workspace release requests and reviews Release
Issue box /v3/issues Where a business owner works a thumbs-down to closed Improve
Environments /v3/environments What each environment runs for an agent, and drift Release
Observability /v3/observability Dashboards, sessions, traces Observe
Memory /v3/memory AgentCore Memory Build
Governance /v3/governance Gateways and Cedar policies Release
My authorizations /v3/connections The current user's own OAuth authorizations —
Gateway tools /v3/tools/gateway The tools the Gateway offers agents, and their targets Build
Spend & alerts /v3/costs Spend per agent, per project and per person, alert thresholds (administrators only) Observe
Project budget /v3/costs?view=project The current project's monthly budget and spend (project members; shown under Show every module) Observe
Department budgets /v3/costs?view=department A department's ceiling and its projects' allocations (department administrators and administrators) Observe
Platform costs /v3/costs?view=platform Every department's budget and the platform's fixed costs (administrators only) Observe
Agent evaluation Evaluation overview /v3/insights Evaluation results at a glance Evaluate
Intent view /v3/intents What people were trying to do, and what the agent could not answer Observe, Improve
Data center /v3/data Datasets and trace data Define, Evaluate
Evaluation tasks /v3/tasks Batch evaluation tasks Evaluate
Online evaluation /v3/online Continuous evaluation of live traffic Observe
Evaluators /v3/evaluators Built-in and custom LLM judges Define, Evaluate
Standards /v3/standards The Agent-DLC workbench: Scorecard, Criteria, Golden set, Admission, Calibration, Release gate, Drift watch, Fix ladder, Decision history Define through Improve
A/B experiments /v3/experiments Configuration experiments and runtime canaries Release
Skill Lab /v3/skill-lab Evaluate and train skills Evaluate
Learn Video introductions /v3/videos Feature walkthrough videos —
Configuration (administrators only; 16 entries) User Management, Administrators /v3/users, /v3/admins Account approval, roles and expiry; administrator accounts Prepare
Projects, Departments, Project settings /v3/projects, /v3/departments, /v3/project-settings The organization structure and project members (the Teams chapter) Prepare
Single sign-on /v3/sso Connect IAM Identity Center or another identity provider Prepare
Fleet, Workspaces /v3/fleet, /v3/workspaces Workspaces (an AWS account + Region) and their bootstrap state Prepare, Release
Network profiles, Storage, Cost tags /v3/network, /v3/storage, /v3/cost-tags Network and storage templates preset for agents; cost-allocation tags (the Platform configuration chapter) Prepare, Observe
Outbound credentials, Announcements, Video management, Models, System update /v3/identity, /v3/announcements, /v3/video-management, /v3/models, /v3/system-update Third-party credentials, in-console announcements and videos, platform default models, online upgrade —

The red box holds the Modules groups (all expanded). 1 The button at the bottom reads Show the everyday modules only, so every module is already shown.

A few things to know up front:

  • With the everyday modules only, Modules keeps Architect assistant, New agent, Agent IDE, Knowledge Bases, Context layer, Releases, Issue box, Observability, Intent view, Standards and Video introductions (administrators also keep the Configuration group).
  • V2 pages opened inside V3: sub-pages V3 has not rebuilt, such as creating a knowledge base, registration forms, editors and an agent's management detail page (/v2/agents?view=detail&id=...), open the V2 page inside the V3 shell at a /v2/... address. The rail still lights the entry they belong to; work on them as usual.
  • The workspace selector at the top right decides which AWS account and Region every request targets. This workshop has a single workspace, default, at tier DEV. Keep it at DEV: a PROD-tier workspace refuses direct agent and criteria changes from members.

5. Check that the environment is ready

5.1 Service status

V3's Command center has no service status card. The Service status card of V2's Workbench opens inside V3: open ConsoleUrl/v2?full=1 in the address bar (full=1 tells V3 to keep this V2 page instead of handing over to the Command center). The V3 shell shows V2's Workbench; scroll down to the Service status card (subtitle "AgentCore control plane").

Expected result:

Row Expected state Meaning
Gateway, Memory, Registry, Observability Ready Created by make bootstrap. "Awaiting bootstrap" means setup did not finish; tell the organiser
Runtime Lights up after the first deploy Counts the agents you deploy; empty on a fresh environment
Policy Attach an engine in Governance Lights up after the Release chapter attaches one in Governance
Evaluation Lights up after the first evaluation Lights up after the Evaluate chapter's evaluation

When you are done, click Launchpad V3 at the top left to return to the Command center.

5.2 Workspace bootstrap status

Open Modules → Configuration → Workspaces in the rail (/v3/workspaces).

Expected result: one row named Default (tagged Hub, with default in small type below it), with Region us-east-1, Tier DEV, and Bootstrap status Ready. This is the same fact as the ticked Workspace ready step of the Command center's launch sequence.

5.3 Backend health check

Open ConsoleUrl/api/health in a new browser tab.

Expected result: a single JSON line, {"status":"ok","version":"0.1.0","region":"us-east-1"} (version is the Launchpad version; 0.1.0 in this run). CloudFront, nginx and the backend are all connected.

5.4 The preset network profile and storage

Open Modules → Configuration → Network profiles (/v3/network), then Configuration → Storage (/v3/storage).

Expected result: the network profile list holds workshop-private with internet access internet through NAT and preflight passed; the storage list holds workshop-files of kind S3 Files with check passed. The deployment template registered both and made them the default project's defaults; once the Platform configuration chapter allows them for 零售客服, participants can pick them directly when they create an agent there. The Platform configuration chapter goes through what each field means.

6. Models: already confirmed by the organiser

This workshop uses the Bedrock models below. When the organiser deployed the environment, the instance's setup script probed each of them with a real Bedrock Converse call, and the organiser checked the result following the Organizer deployment guide before handing you ConsoleUrl, so there is no model check for you to do:

Model id Used by
global.zai.glm-5.3 Every lab agent this workshop creates: lab-service-assistant, lab-policy-advisor, lab-canary-sandbox and the rest, including the BYOC sample that calls Converse
global.openai.gpt-6-sol The judge model of every evaluator
global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5 Only the optional container path, lab-legacy-container

The first time you actually use a model is the first chat after the Build chapter deploys lab-service-assistant: if that chat answers, GLM-5.3 works in your team's account. If it fails with AccessDeniedException then, send a screenshot to the organiser.

On V3's New agent page (/v3/create), the Quick deploy · managed Harness card cannot pick a model: it uses the default model, shown after Deploys with as global.zai.glm-5.3 (the card notes "tools, model and limits are in the full form"). That default is the lab model. The Build chapter creates agents built with Strands Agents, so it goes through Full form or Other ways to build to the full creation form; there Model source defaults to Bedrock and Model to GLM-5.3 (global) (id global.zai.glm-5.3), the first entry in the list. Keep both defaults.

7. Known limitation: LAUNCHPAD_PUBLIC_BASE_URL is not set

The console's public address is the CloudFront domain, and the CloudFront distribution depends on the instance, so the template cannot write that address into the backend configuration at instance boot (it would be a circular dependency). LAUNCHPAD_PUBLIC_BASE_URL therefore keeps its default, and the backend logs a warning at startup.

The setting only matters for as_user (3LO) Identity tools: when an agent calls a third-party OAuth service on behalf of an end user, AgentCore Identity redirects the user's browser back to the console. This workshop uses no as_user tools; sign-in, chat, evaluation, release and observability are unaffected, so there is nothing to do.

Checklist

  • You have your team's ConsoleUrl and the passwords of the five accounts admin, developer, biz-owner, release-ops and sme from the organiser
  • Signed in as admin; the address is ConsoleUrl/v3 and the top left shows Launchpad with a V3 badge
  • The console tour is finished or skipped; the Launch sequence shows 1/5 with Workspace ready ticked
  • The button at the bottom of Modules reads Show the everyday modules only (every module is showing)
  • The workspace at the top right is Default · us-east-1
  • Gateway / Memory / Registry / Observability are Ready in the Service status card at ConsoleUrl/v2?full=1
  • default shows Tier DEV and Bootstrap status Ready under Configuration → Workspaces
  • ConsoleUrl/api/health returns "status":"ok" with region us-east-1
  • Configuration → Network profiles lists workshop-private (preflight passed) and Configuration → Storage lists workshop-files (check passed)

Troubleshooting

Symptom Cause Fix
ConsoleUrl does not load or times out The address was copied wrong, or your team's environment has not finished deploying Check the address starts with https:// and ends with .cloudfront.net; if it still fails, ask the organiser to check your team's stack
A blank page with 403 You reached the instance directly instead of through CloudFront; nginx refuses requests without the origin key Use ConsoleUrl only
The page loads but shows 502 / 503 The backend on the instance is not answering (systemd restarts it 5 seconds after it exits) Refresh and retry; if it persists, ask the organiser to look at the instance (see the troubleshooting section of the Organizer deployment guide)
"Username or password is incorrect." An extra space when copying, or another team's password Copy again from the details the organiser gave your team
Signed in, then immediately back at the sign-in page The browser blocked the session cookie (it is marked Secure and works over HTTPS only) Make sure the address is https://; relax strict privacy settings that block all cookies and retry
You land in V2 (a V2 badge at the top left) or the classic console Back to V2 / Classic console was clicked earlier, or this browser / private window has not opened /v3 yet Open ConsoleUrl/v3
The address is /v2/... but the top bar and rail are V3's V3 has not rebuilt that sub-page and opens the V2 page inside V3 Expected; carry on, and do not click Back to V2
Evaluators, Memory, Governance or similar are missing from the rail Only the everyday modules are showing (the default for member accounts and new private windows), or the group is folded Click Show every module at the bottom of Modules and unfold the group; or press ⌘K and type the page name
The tour card covers the page The tour opens on its own on the first visit to the Command center Click Skip or press Esc; reopen it later from ? → Take the tour
Registry shows "Awaiting bootstrap" make bootstrap did not finish the Registry, or Registry is not available in the Region yet Tell the organiser; the main line does not depend on working the Registry by hand
A chat or an evaluation returns AccessDeniedException Your team's account has no access to that model yet Send a screenshot to the organiser, who enables the model in your team's account

5.4 The preset network profile and storage
